Design wireframe - before app/module changes

Maestro admin pages: first-viewport decision design

Each page must explain status, completeness, risk, and next action without deep scrolling. Long audit trails and implementation details move below the fold or into drawers.

Design principles Admin home Data loaded by dimension Connectors Users and access Notifications Assistant readiness Production readiness PatternOps Reasoning audit Data binding contract QA and test gates
Global ruleNo deep-scroll to understand the page

Perfect top-of-page standard

Every menu page answers one question in the first viewport.

The first screen always has a decision sentence, four scan tiles, one meaningful visual/table, and one next action. Data quality and completeness are shown as operator facts, not internal plumbing. The finished pages must feel board-ready: calm hierarchy, exact labels, balanced spacing, readable tables, and no decorative clutter.

Primary design gate If a Maestro cannot say what is ready, blocked, and next within 10 seconds, the page fails. Review QA gates

4Status tiles max
5-7Rows visible, then expand
0No wave, seed, component names

Architecture and data binding contract

Design must be backed by read-models, not page-local calculations.

The app implementation should keep page components thin. Each menu page receives one typed view-model from the admin broker/data layer. UI renders the view. Tests assert the view-model has enough data to support the first viewport.

PageRequired view-model fieldsLikely current sourceBinding QA

Test strategy

The wireframe becomes acceptance criteria before any module code changes.

Each implementation PR should prove first-viewport clarity, data-binding integrity, tenant isolation, and no jargon in default page copy.

Implementation sequence Approve wireframe, add view-model tests, then change one page at a time. Back to principles
1. Wireframe approvalHTML is reviewed first. No runtime module changes until page intent and data contract are accepted.
2. View-model testsUnit tests assert the data exists: dimensions, counts, percentages, blockers, owners, safe actions, blocked reasons.
3. Rendering testsComponent tests assert first-viewport copy uses operator language and hides implementation labels.
4. Browser smokeAuthenticated Playwright checks 1440x900 and mobile: scrollY starts at 0, top facts visible, no permanent clutter rail.
5. Tenant isolationRun Apex, SkyHarbor, Meridian. Each login/logout cycle confirms active client only and no data leakage.
6. Polish gateDesktop and mobile screenshots must pass visual review for spacing, hierarchy, text fit, table density, and scan quality.
7. Architecture gateComponents cannot compute cross-page facts locally. They render typed read-models from broker/data adapters.
